mappings.note: A definition of 'plateau' as a landform. Not C-SST1.1-LO-2, because the flat-topped upland is described, not explained by any uplift process.

Waterfalls on the steep western face of the Ghats - a relief feature of that range, which the describe-landforms competency covers. Not C-SST1.2-LO-2, since the monsoon here shapes the slope, not anybody's way of life.
Recall that the northern Western Ghats are the Sahyadris - naming a landform. One of the chapter's plain physiography-recall items; the frame has no narrower LO for Indian relief.
Defines 'lagoon' as a coastal landform using Pulicat. Not C-SST1.1-LO-2, because the barrier-bar building process is not what the distractors test.

Contrasts estuary-forming west-coast rivers with delta-forming east-coast rivers, i.e. two different depositional outcomes, so the formation-of-landforms outcome. Not the bare C-SST1.1, because the gradient and sediment behaviour is the reasoning.
Places Barren Island in the Andaman and Nicobar group - identification of a landform and its setting. Not C-SST1.1-LO-2: the volcano is named, its formation is not asked.
Living root bridges are a Khasi response to a very wet climate and flooded streams - environment shaping how people build and move. Not C-SST1.1, because the bridge is human-made, not a landform.
The learner must recognise the Peninsular Plateau from a description of relief and boundaries. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, since no climatic criterion appears among the clues.
The whole claim being tested is that relief shapes climate and culture, which is the interrelationship outcome. Not CG-SST1, because the specific LO already states this link.
Identifies UNESCO as the body recognising the Great Himalayan National Park for its biodiversity - the flora-and-fauna conservation lane. Not C-SST1.1, because no landform is at issue.
Defines 'tributary' as part of a river system, a physical-geography term this competency covers. Not C-SST1.1-LO-2, because no landform is being built in the question.
Directly contrasts the climate of two Himalayan belts, so it is a climatic-region distinction. Not C-SST1.2-LO-2, because nothing about how people live in either belt is required.
Losar and Hemis are Ladakhi festivals, i.e. the cultural life of people in a cold-desert region. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, since the region is the answer but the content tested is its culture.

Rivers of the plains as a source of hydroelectric power - the distribution and use of a resource, which only the goal covers. Not C-SST1.3-LO-3, which asks for conservation sensitivity rather than naming what is generated.

Why population concentrated in the Gangetic Plains - fertile soil supporting agriculture - is the classic environment-to-settlement link. Not C-SST1.1-LO-2, which would be about how the alluvium was laid down rather than who settled on it.

The odd-one-out is 'abundant rainfall', so the item turns on the defining aridity of a desert climatic region. Not C-SST1.1, because the dunes option is the only relief clue and it is a correct, not a keyed, statement.

Places Jaisalmer within the Thar, an arid region, against three other physiographic-climatic regions. Not C-SST1.2-LO-2: the fort's desert adaptation is mentioned in the explanation but the question only asks for the region.
Matching each Himalayan range to its relief character, keyed on the Shivaliks as the transition to the plains. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, because altitude and position, not climate, separate the options.

Why kath-kuni houses survive mild earthquakes is earthquake-preparedness through building practice, which is what the disaster LO asks for. Chosen over C-SST1.2-LO-2, which covers climate-driven housing choices, because the hazard here is seismic, not climatic.

A climate profile - sub -30C winters, negligible rain - has to be matched to the Ladakh cold desert against the hot Thar. That is climatic-region identification, not the C-SST1.1 relief description; note the snow leopard is scenery here, so C-SST1.3-LO-3 would be wrong.

Each option pairs a region with its water regime and the wrong one claims abundant monsoon over the Thar - again a climatic-region property. Not CG-SST1, because the specific climatic LO is available.

The reason statement is rejected because the Aravallis were folded in the distant past, not raised by recent volcanism, so the item tests formation processes. Not C-SST1.1, since the age claim alone would not decide the key.

Statement-set recall about coral Lakshadweep, the size of the Andaman archipelago and Barren Island - island identification. Not C-SST1.1-LO-1: coral is mentioned as an island's material in passing, not as a rock-type classification.
Defines 'peninsula'. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, because nothing has to be located; the distractors are other coastal terms.
Names a forest-dwelling community of the plateau, tying a group's way of life to its physical setting. Not C-SST1.1, because the plateau is only the backdrop and the answer is a people.

Reasons from brackish river-sea-land mixing to a mangrove ecosystem, i.e. the earth as a habitat for other forms of life, which only the goal states. Not C-SST1.3-LO-3, because nothing about conserving the Sundarbans is asked.

Mawlynnong is identified precisely as the village famed for community cleanliness and waste practices, which is the prevent-pollution lane. Not C-SST1.3-LO-3, which is about conserving natural resources rather than keeping surroundings clean.
Highest versus lowest Himalayan range - a relief comparison. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, because the keyed difference is altitude, and the climate-flavoured distractors are all wrong.
Matching features to descriptions, keyed on the Deccan as flat highland. Not C-SST1.2-LO-2, even though a kath-kuni house is a distractor, since the correct pairing is a landform description.
The wrinkling-carpet analogy is an explanation of how the collision crumpled and raised the range, so formation of landforms. Not C-SST1.1, because no feature is being named or described.

Although the Cellular Jail is a freedom-struggle site, the question only asks which island group holds it, so it is island identification. CG-SST2 would be wrong: this frame's history goal covers medieval kingdoms, temples and bhakti, not the colonial period.
A cluster of climate and altitude clues has to be resolved to the Ladakh region against the Western Ghats, Sundarbans and Rann. That is climatic-region placement, not C-SST1.1 landform description.

The wrong pairing claims rainforest cover over the Gangetic Plains, a vegetation-and-rainfall property of the region. Not C-SST1.1, because the discriminating fact is climatic rather than a matter of relief.

The reason - sediment deposition by the Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri - is the formation mechanism of the east-coast deltas. Not C-SST1.2-LO-2, because fertility is asserted, not linked to any farming population.

Statement set on the relative height of the two Ghats, the cross-border extent of the Sundarbans and India's southern ocean boundary - locational and relief facts. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, because none of the three statements concerns climate.

Names 'kunds' as the other Rajasthani rainwater store, keeping it in the water-conservation lane alongside the taanka item. Not C-SST1.2-LO-2, because the point of these structures is saving a scarce resource rather than illustrating desert life generally.

Defines 'flora and fauna', the exact vocabulary the conservation outcome is written in, and the item frames it as a region's biodiversity. Not CG-SST1, since the more specific conservation LO names plant and animal life directly.

Attributes the continuing rise of the Himalayas to ongoing plate convergence - a formation process, with erosion and volcanism offered as rival mechanisms. Not C-SST1.1, which would only need the range described as it stands.

Locates Darjeeling in the Lower Himalayan belt within West Bengal, against three other hill stations - a placement fact. Not C-SST1.2-LO-2, because why hill stations exist where they do is not asked, only which one is in that state.
